newsitem.title: UK: Wet N.Sea market quiet as outright loses ground.
newsitem.headline: Wet N.Sea market quiet as outright loses ground.

text.p: North Sea crude markets saw little action on Monday afternoon as outright Brent eased and traders waited for a solid indication of the Dated Brent level.
This week's CFDs lost a few cents to trade at -4 cents while next week's Sept 16-20 were discussed around -11/-8 cents, down three cents from early talk.
Oct Brent shed 20 cents to talk at $22.34 per barrel by 1532 GMT, and there was little interest in the Sept/Oct spread discussed around +55/60 cents.
Apart from Brent the rest of the North Sea sweet grades were assessed unchanged from the end of last week.

Sellers of physical Brent cargoes were also wide apart with one major offering at a five cent premium to October and a trader five cents firmer. This followed Friday's deal at October Brent -7 cents for a Sept 13-15 cargo.
Intermonth talk further out saw buyers and sellers slightly closer with Oct/Nov at +67/68 cents and Nov/Dec +60/63 cents.
Mediterranean crude rallied on strong downstream demand and continued loading delays at Russia's Novorossiisk terminal in the Black Sea.
Russia's Urals was valued at Dated Brent -85/75 cif Augusta, 10 cents above one week ago.
Berthing at Novorossiisk was suspended over the weekend due to bad weather, exacerbating the existing 5-6 day delay due to pipeline maintenance in September, dealers said.
Some traders emphasised the importance of these delays in the recent price rise, and another said it was mostly linked to the recent surge in gas oil prices.
But another said: "It's more to do with the strength of high sulphur fuel oil in the Med."
